classification.difficultyReason: Identify excluded denominator values, choose a common denominator, rearrange the resulting equation and factorise a non-monic quadratic before checking admissibility. These are several linked but explicitly taught procedures.

answer.worked:
Restrictions: $x\ne-\frac74,-7$. Multiply by $(4x+7)(x+7)$.

$$\begin{align*}(3x+1)(x+7)&=(4x+7)(x+7)-6(4x+7)\\3x^2+22x+7&=4x^2+11x+7\\x^2-11x&=0\\x(x-11)&=0\\x&=0\text{ or }x=11\end{align*}$$

Both values satisfy the original equation and its denominator restrictions.

Restrictions: $x\ne1,-2,0$. Multiply by $x(x-1)(x+2)$.

$$\begin{align*}4x(x+2)-5x(x-1)&=3(x-1)(x+2)\\-x^2+13x&=3x^2+3x-6\\4x^2-10x-6&=0\\2x^2-5x-3&=0\\(2x+1)(x-3)&=0\\x&=-\frac12\text{ or }x=3\end{align*}$$

Both values satisfy the original equation and its denominator restrictions.

Restrictions: $x\ne4,-3$. Multiply by $3(x-4)(x+3)$.

$$\begin{align*}3(x+4)(x+3)+3(x-3)(x-4)&=16(x-4)(x+3)\\6x^2+72&=16x^2-16x-192\\10x^2-16x-264&=0\\5x^2-8x-132&=0\\5x^2-30x+22x-132&=0\\5x(x-6)+22(x-6)&=0\\(x-6)(5x+22)&=0\\x&=6\text{ or }x=-\frac{22}{5}\end{align*}$$

Both values satisfy the original equation and its denominator restrictions.

Restrictions: $x\ne\frac72,3$. Cross-multiply.

$$\begin{align*}(x+3)(x-3)&=(2x-1)(2x-7)\\x^2-9&=4x^2-16x+7\\3x^2-16x+16&=0\\3x^2-12x-4x+16&=0\\3x(x-4)-4(x-4)&=0\\(3x-4)(x-4)&=0\\x&=\frac43\text{ or }x=4\end{align*}$$

Both values satisfy the original equation and its denominator restrictions.
